message.content:
Below is a list of the **long‑weekend holidays that occurred in Canada during 2023**.  
A long weekend is defined as a holiday that creates a three‑day break (Friday‑Saturday‑Sunday or Friday‑Saturday‑Monday) or a four‑day break (Thursday‑Friday‑Saturday‑Sunday or Friday‑Saturday‑Sunday‑Monday).  

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Province(s) where it was observed | Long‑weekend type | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-----------------------------------|-------------------|-------|
| **Jan 2** | New Year’s Day (observed) | All provinces & territories | 4‑day (Thu‑Fri‑Sat‑Sun) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday, so it was observed on Monday. |
| **Feb 20** | Family Day | Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario (except Toronto) | 3‑day (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) | Third Monday in February. |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | All provinces & territories | 3‑day (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) | Good Friday is a statutory holiday nationwide. |
| **May 24** | Victoria Day | All provinces & territories | 3‑day (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) | Celebrated on the last Monday before May 25. |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | All provinces & territories | 3‑day (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) | First Monday in September. |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | All provinces & territories | 3‑day (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) | Second Monday in October. |
| **Dec 23** | Christmas Day | All provinces & territories | 3‑day (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) | Christmas fell on Monday. |
| **Dec 26** | Boxing Day | All provinces & territories | 3‑day (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) | Boxing Day fell on Tuesday, but the preceding Friday (Dec 23) and Saturday (Dec 24) are part of the Christmas long weekend. |

### How to use this list in your app

1. **Store the dates** in a calendar or holiday‑API database.  
2. **Flag the long‑weekend holidays** so your UI can highlight them.  
3. **Add province‑specific logic** if you want to show only the holidays that apply to a user’s province (e.g., Family Day only for Alberta, BC, Saskatchewan, and Ontario).  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the list broken down by province or if you need additional details (e.g., exact start/end times, public‑service closures, etc.).
